title: Meister Eckhart, Vol. 1
author: Meister Eckhart (Evans trans)
description: Meister Eckhart, Volume 1, translated by C. de B. Evans (London: John M. Watkins, 1924) from the edition of Franz Pfeiffer (Leipzig, 1857), 'with some omissions and additions'. Eckhart von Hochheim (c. 1260-1328), Dominican friar, Paris master and preacher, is the greatest of the German mystics, and some of his propositions were condemned in 1329. This volume gathers his German sermons and collations, presenting his central teachings: the birth of the Word in the ground of the soul, the 'spark' or uncreated something in the soul, detachment (Abgeschiedenheit) and letting-be (Gelassenheit), the distinction between God and the Godhead beyond God, the breakthrough into the silent desert of the divine essence, and living 'without a why'. The Evans translation was the main English Eckhart for decades and influenced Theosophical, Traditionalist and comparative interest in him alongside Vedanta and Zen.
